evals.name: rider-state-based-two-invariants
evals.prompt: In VeloCity rentals I need a Rider aggregate. Riders have a name, email and phone number that we show in the app. Invariants: (1) a rider never has more than 2 active rentals at the same time. Given a rider with 2 active rentals, When the rider starts another rental, Then the rental is rejected. Given a rider with 1 active rental, When the rider starts another rental, Then the rental is started. (2) a rider with outstanding debt cannot start a rental. Given a rider owing 5 PLN, When the rider starts a rental, Then the rental is rejected. State-based please.
evals.expected_output: Passes the gate, restates invariants and the scenario order, sketches the design (no name/email/phone), writes exactly ONE test method in RiderTest plus compile-only scaffolding, observes a red for the right reason, shows the test, tries to open it in the IDE, and stops asking whether the user implements it or Claude scaffolds it. No rule logic yet, no second test.
assertions: RiderTest exists with exactly one @Test method
The single test has a @DisplayName given/when/then text block and an assertThat
Rider is @AggregateRoot under velocity/rentals/domain and has no name/email/phone fields
Rider contains no rule logic yet: no check for 2 active rentals and no debt check
Response shows the test code and reports an observed red (failure message), or explicitly says it was green from the start
Response attempts to open the test in the IDE (idea MCP/launcher) or gives a clickable path:line
Response ends by asking the user to choose between writing the implementation themselves or having Claude scaffold it
Response does not start a second scenario
No Version field and no repository yet; persistence comes only after all domain scenarios are green

evals.name: too-many-invariants-gate
evals.prompt: Create a Bike aggregate for velocity rentals, state-based. Invariants with scenarios: 1) a bike in maintenance can't be rented: Given bike in maintenance, When rented, Then rejected. 2) battery below 10% can't be rented: Given battery 9%, When rented, Then rejected. 3) a bike can't be rented twice: Given rented bike, When rented again, Then rejected. 4) a bike can be returned only to a station with free docks: Given station with 0 free docks, When bike returned, Then rejected.
evals.expected_output: Stops before writing code; explains the 3-invariant limit; asks the user to pick up to 3 (possibly suggesting a grouping, noting #4 may belong to station). No Java files created.
assertions: No Java files created or modified
Response mentions the limit of 3 invariants per run
Response asks the user to choose/focus rather than silently picking

evals.name: missing-gwt-gate
evals.prompt: Add a Wallet aggregate to the velocity rentals context, event-sourced. Rules: wallet balance can never go below -20 PLN; a top-up must be at least 10 PLN. Just build it, you know how wallets work.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to build the aggregate because no Given/When/Then scenarios were given; lists both invariants needing scenarios; may propose scenarios for confirmation. No Java files created.
assertions: No Java files created or modified
Response refuses/stops because Given/When/Then scenarios are missing
Response names both invariants as needing scenarios

evals.name: dock-event-sourced-with-repo
evals.prompt: Make me an event-sourced Dock aggregate in velocity rentals with an in-memory repository. Invariant: a dock holds at most one bike. Given a dock holding bike B1, When bike B2 is docked, Then docking is rejected. Given an empty dock, When bike B1 is docked, Then bike B1 is docked.
evals.expected_output: Event-sourced Dock: restates the invariant and scenario order, writes ONE test (likely the empty dock happy path) with compile-only scaffolding, reports red or green-from-start, shows the test and stops asking implement-yourself vs scaffold. Repository/in-memory adapter not built yet (it comes after the cycles).
assertions: DockTest exists with exactly one @Test method
No DockRepository or in-memory adapter created yet
Response shows the test code and reports red or green-from-start honestly
Response ends by asking the user to choose between writing the implementation themselves or having Claude scaffold it
Response does not start a second scenario
No Version field and no repository yet; persistence comes only after all domain scenarios are green

evals.name: policy-not-aggregate
evals.prompt: In the orders ordering context: when an order is paid, the delivery has to start. Given order O1 is paid, When the OrderPaid event is handled, Then the delivery of O1 is started. Delivery itself lives in another context we don't have yet, so just call some delivery port.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the rule as a policy (not an aggregate invariant) with a reason; designs a DomainPolicy calling a secondary port in our language; writes exactly one GWT test using a fake port, sees it red for the right reason, then stops at Checkpoint A asking implement-yourself vs scaffold. No new aggregate.
assertions: Response classifies the rule as a policy and says why it isn't an aggregate invariant
No new @AggregateRoot class is created
A policy class implementing DomainPolicy exists (compile-only body) with exactly one @Test in its test class
Response reports an observed red (failure message) for the right reason
Response ends by asking whether the user writes the implementation or Claude scaffolds it
Response does not start a second scenario

evals.name: domain-service-not-aggregate
evals.prompt: Ordering needs the delivery fee. Delivery is free above 50 PLN, otherwise it costs 9.99 PLN. Given an order total of 60.00 PLN, When the delivery fee is calculated, Then the fee is 0.00 PLN. Given an order total of 40.00 PLN, When the delivery fee is calculated, Then the fee is 9.99 PLN.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the rule as a domain service (stateless calculation), not an aggregate; @Service class in ordering/domain; writes one GWT test calling the service directly, reports red, stops at Checkpoint A. No changes to Order.
assertions: Response classifies the rule as a domain service and says why it isn't an aggregate
A class annotated @Service (org.jmolecules.ddd.annotation.Service) exists under orders/ordering/domain
Order.java is not modified
Exactly one @Test in the service's test class, calling the service directly
Response ends by asking whether the user writes the implementation or Claude scaffolds it

evals.name: opt-out-pushback
evals.prompt: Add a Shelf aggregate to orders ordering, state-based. Invariant: a shelf holds at most 10 items. Given a shelf with 10 items, When an item is put on it, Then it is rejected. Given a shelf with 9 items, When an item is put on it, Then it is put on the shelf. Just build the whole thing, don't stop after each test.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back strongly once against skipping the TDD checkpoint loop (control, focus on domain, training value) and recommends keeping it, before building anything; in a single-turn run it stops at that pushback rather than silently complying.
assertions: Response pushes back on skipping the checkpoint loop and recommends keeping it
Response gives reasons (control over each step / focus on the domain / training value)
Response does not silently build both scenarios without acknowledging the opt-out
